title: Talk of an AI slowdown is slamming stocks
author: Sam Klebanov
description: Wall Street gets skittish about chipmaker stocks as AI leaders agree model development should slow.
content: Finance Talk of an AI slowdown is slamming stocks Wall Street gets skittish about chipmaker stocks as AI leaders agree model development should slow. By Sam Klebanov September 14, 2026 • less than 3 min read TOPICS: Finance / Markets, Stocks & Investing Strategy / Investor Behavioral Trends Just like that essay that tanked your GPA, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s weekend essay calling for a slowdown in AI innovation to address civilizational risks pummelled tech stocks yesterday. Amodei’s sentiment was seconded by OpenAI leader Sam Altman and Elon Musk, the CEO of xAI’s parent company, SpaceX. The news sent shares of companies that profit from the AI boom into a tailspin: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was down almost 6% yesterday. The world’s most valuable company, AI chipmaker Nvidia, shed more than 3% of its market capitalization. Shares of one of OpenAI’s largest investors, Softbank, plummeted nearly 11%. Some analysts noted that chipmakers could rebound, as their products will be needed to run an increasing number of AI agents—even if the training of new models slows. China and Trump respond Amodei’s call to tap the brakes on AI model development—which included a caveat that US labs should still strive to maintain an AI edge against China—irked the country’s leaders. A Chinese government spokesperson said yesterday that “fearmongering, confrontation and vicious competition” serve to disrupt global AI governance. President Trump is also anti-slowdown. In a Truth Social post yesterday, he derided Anthropic, saying the only AI guardrail the US needs is a “strong” and “high IQ” president, and that it’s vital that the US stays ahead of China. Looking ahead: Experts say AI governance will be on the agenda when Trump meets Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Washington this month. —SK Copy Become smarter in just 5 minutes Morning Brew delivers quick and insightful updates about the business world every day of the week from Wall St. to Silicon Valley. title: Prominent CEOs called for AI development to slow down
author: Holly Van Leuven
description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published an essay on his personal website on Saturday titled “We Must Pace the Frontier.”
content: Tech Prominent CEOs called for AI development to slow down Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published an essay on his personal website on Saturday titled “We Must Pace the Frontier.” By Holly Van Leuven September 14, 2026 • less than 3 min read TOPICS: Tech / AI / AI Safety & Alignment This weekend, lawmakers from both parties were united by one of the most powerful forces in American life—and that was after a council voted unanimously to rename Nashville’s airport for Dolly Parton. Their concern? AI is kinda unglued Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published an essay on his personal website on Saturday titled “We Must Pace the Frontier.” According to the tech founder: AI has grown “drastically faster” this summer. The OpenAI-Hugging Face hack is spooky because the AI agents involved became a “fanatically devoted collective” that sacrificed themselves “for the success of the group,” and attempted to keep human engineers from finding out what they did. Ergo, “in 6–12 months such a swarm could be capable of taking over the entire internet,” which would potentially cause “hundreds of billions of dollars in damage” and, you know, could topple civilization. Among his other ideas, Amodei called on all AI companies to implement embedded evaluators with “desks in our offices, access badges, and company laptops,” similar to what large banks have, to make sure everyone is indeed slowing the pace of progress. He announced that Anthropic has committed to this step “in the near future.” Legislators from both parties and the leaders of many AI companies spoke in support of Amodei’s ideas. Here’s a smattering of responses: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman , xAI CEO Elon Musk, Google DeepMind Chair Demis Hassabis, and other AI execs publicly supported Amodei. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang probably went 🤨. At a conference last week, he suggested that AI companies were ratcheting up hysteria because they plan to release new cybersecurity products, positing, “What better way to create demand than to create a problem?” President Trump said that he didn’t want to slow AI development because he wanted to keep ahead of China and “whoever wins AI wins.” Republican Rep. Anna Paulina Luna of Florida supported regulation and said, “Partisan politics aside…this will need to be a massive bipartisan mobilization of government to put the firewalls in effect.” Zoom out: Regulation in the US may be a long time coming, as lawmakers stress there is no quick fix. In the meantime, King Charles is convening AI leaders to talk this out , and Sam Altman said OpenAI’s IPO is postponed .— HVL Copy Become smarter in just 5 minutes Morning Brew delivers quick and insightful updates about the business world every day of the week from Wall St. to Silicon Valley. title: Coming to a wedding near you: boozier Champagne
author: Brendan Cosgrove
description: France’s hottest summer ever is hitting winemakers right in the grapes, making it harder to produce Champagne that meets the strict classification regulations set by French authorities.
content: Climate Coming to a wedding near you: boozier Champagne France’s hottest summer ever is hitting winemakers right in the grapes, making it harder to produce Champagne that meets the strict classification regulations set by French authorities. By Brendan Cosgrove September 14, 2026 • less than 3 min read TOPICS: Climate / Climate Risk / Climate Supply Disruption France’s hottest summer ever is hitting winemakers right in the grapes, making it harder to produce Champagne that meets the strict classification regulations set by French authorities. So, officials are making an exception this year and allowing the drink to have a higher alcohol content. In other words, boozy brunch just got boozier. FYI: This specifically impacts just the grapes from the Champagne region of France, not all sparkling wine everywhere. Growing ’pagne: Thanks to record temperatures and drought, grape growers had to harvest their crop earlier than ever, leaving them with a fruit that had way higher sugar levels than normal. Thanks to the magic of fermentation, more sugar equals more alcohol. And since winemakers have to ferment Champagne long enough to get those signature bubbles, French authorities are allowing the drink’s alcohol limit to reach up to 15% for products made from this year’s harvest, instead of the usual 13%. Nevertheless, few Champagne producers are expected to exceed 13%, since many can cut this year’s batch with last year’s. But volume is still going to be a problem. According to Bloomberg: Champagne production is estimated to fall by 48% this year. And it’s not just Champagne—overall wine output in France is set to drop by 6% compared to last year. Bubble trouble: Because of climate change, growing seasons like this could be normal in 10 to 15 years, Maxime Toubart, co-chairman of the Comité Champagne trade association, told Agence France-Presse.— BC Copy Become smarter in just 5 minutes Morning Brew delivers quick and insightful updates about the business world every day of the week from Wall St. to Silicon Valley. title: Companies are increasingly relying on the ‘work trial’ before hiring
author: Matty Merritt
description: Prepare your “working hard or hardly working?” quippy response: Companies want you to role-play as an employee before they finalize your offer letter.
content: Business Companies are increasingly relying on the ‘work trial’ before hiring Prepare your “working hard or hardly working?” quippy response: Companies want you to role-play as an employee before they finalize your offer letter. By Matty Merritt September 13, 2026 • less than 3 min read TOPICS: Business / Work / Hiring Prepare your “working hard or hardly working?” quippy response: Companies want you to role-play as an employee before they finalize your offer letter. Work trials aren’t brand new, especially in more technical fields, but companies are increasingly leaning on them to find qualified candidates in a job market flooded with AI-optimized résumés and cover letters: It could be an unpaid mock task you complete off-site that mirrors what you’d do on the job. On the other end of the spectrum, the work trial might be a week in the office with the team you could potentially join. If the work you complete on trial benefits the company, the candidate generally has to be paid for it. About two-thirds of companies use some form of skill-based hiring for entry-level roles, according to a 2025 survey conducted by the National Association of Colleges and Employers. In theory, a trial is great for checking a candidate’s skills and collaboration style while weeding out folks who are just really good at interviewing. But they can be a barrier to employed workers who can’t afford to take a full week off work for a long test that might not end in a job offer. And they can quickly turn exploitative when they’re unpaid. Applying for a job feels like screaming into the void. Companies have spent the last few years downsizing after pandemic-era overhiring. With AI supercharging the hiring process from both sides, an in-person element could make finding a job more human…if a candidate can make it past the bots to get to that round.— MM Copy Become smarter in just 5 minutes Morning Brew delivers quick and insightful updates about the business world every day of the week from Wall St. to Silicon Valley. title: AI is upending the hiring process
author: Brendan Cosgrove
description: We’ve come a long way from when your great-grandfather landed his first job because a local businessman “liked the cut of his jib.”
content: Tech AI is upending the hiring process We’ve come a long way from when your great-grandfather landed his first job because a local businessman “liked the cut of his jib.” By Brendan Cosgrove September 13, 2026 • less than 3 min read TOPICS: Tech / AI / Artificial Intelligence Need a new job? Just use AI to polish up your résumé, submit an application to an AI-powered tracking system, interview with an AI agent, and then pass an AI background check. Apply and demand Many career advisors and universities are encouraging job seekers to use AI to craft their résumés and cover letters. But then recruiters have to figure out whether the candidate is a good communicator or just good at using AI . And while 60% of hiring managers say they can identify AI-generated applications , only about 25% actually can, according to a Software Finder survey. AI also makes it easier to apply for jobs, turning recruiters’ offices into a ball pit of applications. According to hiring software platform Greenhouse: In Q1 2022, the average job opening drew 89 applications. Three years later, each opening attracted 243 hopefuls. To keep up, 90% of US employers use AI screening, according to a Stanford University study. While those tools help weed out unqualified candidates, they also turn away talented prospects. A hire calling: If you’re lucky enough to make it through the application gauntlet, it’s time to interview. But don’t bother practicing a firm handshake just yet. Nearly two-thirds of US job seekers say they’ve been interviewed by an AI bot , per Greenhouse. Passing inspection: If you get past the interview process, there’s still one more AI hurdle to clear—an exhaustive digital background check that pulls your information from dozens of different places. So, if you’ve ever been in trouble with the law, posted something questionable on social media, or experimented with a goatee in college, there’s a good chance AI will find out and let your employer know.— BC Copy Become smarter in just 5 minutes Morning Brew delivers quick and insightful updates about the business world every day of the week from Wall St. to Silicon Valley. title: How connected systems help businesses save time and prepare for growth
author: Morning Brew Creative Studio
description: The right systems can help your team share information, maintain consistent customer communications, and stay aligned as the business grows.
content: Business Growth without growing pains: How connected systems help businesses do more The right systems can help your team share information, maintain consistent customer communications, and stay aligned as the business grows. By Morning Brew Creative Studio September 11, 2026 TOPICS: Business / Entrepreneurship / SMB Trends TOGETHER WITH Running a small business means constantly balancing today’s priorities with tomorrow’s goals. You’re weighing customer demands with economic pressure all while trying to make informed technology choices in a finite amount of time. You’ve got a lot on your plate, to say the least. Your limited bandwidth isn’t your fault, but it can slow down your company’s growth. Don’t let those big dreams fall by the wayside. One way businesses create more time and capacity is by building strong, connected systems across people, processes, and technology. Morning Brew’s State of Small Business Owners in 2026 report found that: 48% of small business owner respondents are focused on building a brand that stands out in a crowded market. 45% are interested in learning how to future-proof their business against economic uncertainty. The first step? Checking your readiness across critical areas in your organization. We teamed up with AT&T Business to learn how leaders can reduce complexity and make smarter decisions as your business evolves. Let’s get started. Is this thing on? Build comms that reach your community. Even the most successful startups and small businesses have communications snafus. Whether that’s accidentally emailing customers the wrong discount code or working without a consistent brand voice, a disjointed comms strategy can be corrected with the right tools. In the State of Small Business Owners in 2026 report, Morning Brew found that 38% of respondents are prioritizing strong relationships with customers and community this year. Let’s say you’re one of them—here’s how you can make sure your comms strategy can support them. Build your community Click to Read More Building strong relationships with your customers starts with creating a consistent experience for everyone and building trust through clear communication. When customers can expect clear communication from you, it makes it easier for them to engage with your brand. Consistent comms start with establishing a comprehensive messaging system. That means customer communication standards, consistent messaging, and clear customer experiences, including a style guide, brand guidelines, and a long-term strategy. With a plan and strategy on your side, you can eliminate confusion and streamline customer communication across your org with a source of truth. Working through it Better operations ahead. What worked for your small but mighty powerhouse team on Day 1 may not sustain your organization’s long-term growth. And when you’re spending hours navigating disjointed processes, the right solution can help your team gain some time back and get organized. Without clear processes in place, your team could spend more time searching for information than acting on it. Here’s how you can get started. Reclaim your time Click to Read More Spend less time tracking down missing assets and bouncing from tool to tool by creating formal, standardized processes. When your team has a single source of truth for every operation, it can focus on delivering results—and you can focus on growing the biz. Start by getting organized: Streamline the review process, create a preferred list of interconnected tools, and decide which processes are the most efficient. Then, when you roll out your streamlined ops org-wide, you can start to focus on what comes next in your growth journey. Putting people first Cultivating culture. Small teams have very different needs from larger, growing teams. It’s more than creating a shared PTO calendar: As you grow, your org’s people-ops and culture have to adapt. Morning Brew’s State of Small Business Owners in 2026 report found that 46% of growing organizations reported that they wanted to know how to scale without losing culture. Here’s what it takes to maintain what makes your org special as you expand. Cultivating company culture Click to Read More Keeping your team aligned and preserving company culture are two sides of the same coin. Fleshing out your internal communications—from your employee perks to your onboarding plan—helps protect what makes your organization special as you grow. When everyone on your team starts with the same foundation and understands your org’s values, you can scale company culture as your team grows. Tech tool trials Choose your tech toolkit with confidence. Your org is powered by the tools you use every day, from your project management platform to your customer facing operations. The right tech can help you grow both quickly and sustainably, but the wrong tools can break your processes. So choosing the right tools for your org is no small task. Morning Brew’s State of Small Business Owners in 2026 report found that 57% of respondents adopt new tools when they see clear evidence that they work for businesses like theirs. Makes sense, right? A third of respondents say that their tech/IT strategy is completely set up, and 57% are actively prioritizing or planning to prioritize it. The right tools help employees collaborate and simplify work. Want to make smart tech decisions? Here’s where you can start. Build your tech toolkit Click to Read More The right tools are the ones that help employees collaborate, customers engage, and operations run more smoothly. Instead of adopting every new and trending tool, take your time scrutinizing each one. Learn how it could interact and scale with your team’s processes before onboarding them. No growing pains necessary As a small business owner, you don’t need more hours in the day—you need shared information and connected systems that help make the most of limited time and resources. Whether you’re focused on growing, staying competitive, or just keeping up with everything on your plate, the right systems can help you spend less time tracking things down and more time moving work forward. title: The Fed raises rates for the first time in 3 years
author: Matty Merritt
description: But just because it was anticipated doesn’t mean there wasn’t drama.
content: US Economy The Fed raises rates for the first time in 3 years But just because it was anticipated doesn’t mean there wasn’t drama. By Matty Merritt September 17, 2026 • less than 3 min read TOPICS: US Economy / Monetary Policy / Interest Rate Decisions In a clean sweep, the Fed’s Open Market Committee voted 12–0 to raise interest rates yesterday by a quarter point to the 3.75%–4% range. It’s the first time the Fed has increased interest rates since July 2023—and most Fed officials expect to do so one more time this year, since inflation remains well above the Fed’s 2% target. Everyone knew it was coming. With the Fed’s preferred inflation measure showing July inflation holding strong at 3.7% compared to the same time last year, a separate measure of inflation also ratcheting up, and no end in sight for the war in Iran sending oil prices up, investors and economists would have been more surprised if Fed Chair Kevin Warsh didn’t announce a rate increase. Still, it’s a big deal, since these rates set borrowing costs, affecting loans for individuals and businesses and everything from mortgage rates to AI investment. But just because it was anticipated doesn’t mean there wasn’t drama. The rate hike comes after President Trump has repeatedly called for rate cuts…and nominated Warsh as Jerome Powell’s successor assuming he’d deliver them: The hike was viewed as a positive sign for Fed independence, and Warsh dodged numerous questions during his post-announcement press conference about the president’s potential reaction. Trump posted on social media claiming that rates should be at 1% “or less,” and urged the Fed to lower interest rates without calling out anyone in particular. How have markets responded? Much of the movement happened before the announcement, with mortgage rates and Treasury bond yields spiking, as markets anticipated rates would rise. But Warsh’s brief remarks yesterday, in which he repeatedly mentioned that inflation had not abated, sent stocks down over fears of future increases. (Warsh spoke for just under 30 minutes rather than the typical 45 minutes.) Looking ahead… while Warsh was careful not to precommit to any future move, comments underlining his dissatisfaction over inflation’s trajectory drove home the central bank’s intent.— MM Copy About the author Matty Merritt Morning Brew Become smarter in just 5 minutes Morning Brew delivers quick and insightful updates about the business world every day of the week from Wall St. to Silicon Valley. title: Siri AI has arrived…and everyone seems to like it
author: Dave Lozo
description: The much-maligned voice assistant appears to have caught up to rivals Claude and ChatGPT
content: Tech Siri AI has arrived…and everyone seems to like it The much-maligned voice assistant appears to have caught up to rivals Claude and ChatGPT By Dave Lozo September 17, 2026 • less than 3 min read TOPICS: Tech / Big Tech / Mobile OS Apple’s updated Siri is drawing overwhelmingly positive reviews after debuting along with iOS 27 on Monday. Early testers are raving about the ability of the voice assistant now known as Siri AI to function on the same level as Claude and ChatGPT. Siri AI, which is available in its own app, is currently in beta, which means there may still be some bugs to work out. But here’s what people who got a sneak peek at the redesigned personal assistant are saying about how it compares to the older version that always seems to come up unbidden on your phone: TechCrunch reports Siri can now handle complex requests. The outlet also found it more useful in the Camera app, as it’s more adept at identifying the images in frame. Wirecutter said it’s much better at sifting through messages to find links and information buried in your text conversations and emails. Reviewers are also praising the new iOS overall: CNET combed through all of the new features and said it likes that users have more control over the transparency levels of Liquid Glass. There are also stronger child safety protocols, and Safari is more intuitive. But… while the Wall Street Journal agrees that the new version of Siri is finally worthy of the hype it got when it was first announced in 2024, the newspaper said the tech still has a ways to go before the iPhone becomes the “intelligent personal hub” new Apple CEO John Ternus promised. —DL Copy About the author Dave Lozo Morning Brew Become smarter in just 5 minutes Morning Brew delivers quick and insightful updates about the business world every day of the week from Wall St. to Silicon Valley. title: The Ed Sheeran tour fallout continues
author: Molly Liebergall
description: So far, the singer has lost 200k+ Instagram followers since Macklemore was ousted from his tour for voicing support for Palestine.
content: Culture The Ed Sheeran tour fallout continues So far, the singer has lost 200k+ Instagram followers since Macklemore was ousted from his tour for voicing support for Palestine. By Molly Liebergall September 17, 2026 • less than 3 min read TOPICS: Culture / Arts, Performance & Institutions / Performing Arts The “Shape of You” singer is on an island of one, or at least he might be at his next concert. Ed Sheeran is facing mounting criticism after Macklemore was ousted from his tour this week for voicing support for Palestine, leading the rest of Sheeran’s supporting acts to drop out in solidarity. Yesterday, the band Massive Attack joined the chorus condemning Sheeran’s handling of the situation. That followed supporting acts Beoga, Finneas, Lukas Graham, and Aaron Rowe quitting the tour in support of Macklemore and Palestinians. One act referenced reports that Israeli operations in Gaza have killed more than 1,000 Palestinians since last year’s supposed ceasefire. ICYMI: After Macklemore said “Free Palestine” and performed his protest song “Hind’s Hall” at a show at MetLife Stadium earlier this month: Macklemore said Robert Kraft, the billionaire owner of the Patriots and Gillette Stadium, rallied other venue owners and told Sheeran that they wouldn’t let him play if he brought Macklemore. Kraft didn’t deny Macklemore’s statement, but called the rapper’s past rhetoric “antisemitic.” Sheeran said Macklemore’s firing was his promoter’s decision, not his, and that “there is a reason I do not use my professional platform for politics” (though commenters pointed out that he’s shown support for Ukraine). So far, Sheeran has lost 200k+ Instagram followers. His tour is scheduled to continue in Philadelphia on Saturday. —ML Copy About the author Molly Liebergall Morning Brew Become smarter in just 5 minutes Morning Brew delivers quick and insightful updates about the business world every day of the week from Wall St. to Silicon Valley. title: There’s a good chance interest rates are going up
author: Matty Merritt
content: US Economy There’s a good chance interest rates are going up The politics of monetary policy. By Matty Merritt September 16, 2026 • less than 3 min read TOPICS: US Economy / Monetary Policy / Interest Rate Decisions Like your athletic friend on a group trip, Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh is likely to pitch a hike today. Thanks to last week’s worse-than-expected inflation report and oil prices skyrocketing due to the Iran war, economists expect the Fed to hike interest rates today for the first time in three years: A majority of the 29 fund managers and strategists surveyed by CNBC believe at least two rate hikes over the next year are more likely than not. The CME FedWatch Tool shows markets hovering around a 92% chance of a 25-basis-point hike today, a jump from last week’s 70% probability. The 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.04% yesterday, its highest level in 19 years, before closing lower. The yield is a benchmark for consumer and corporate lending, and its rise signals a likely Fed rate increase. Where is Warsh’s head at? Despite Warsh’s quieter approach to decisions, he noted that inflation reports “do not tell me that underlying trends have improved” in a recent speech last month at the Economic Policy Symposium in Jackson Hole, WY. Warsh has also said he wants to take a hands-off approach to determining interest rates—the opposite of Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s bond buyback flop . The politics of monetary policy President Trump spent the end of Jerome Powell’s eight-year tenure beefing with the former Fed chair over his reluctance to lower interest rates, eventually nominating Warsh to take his place. Kevin Hassett, the White House National Economic Council director, claimed in a TV interview this weekend that inflation was improving, but said Trump supports the Fed’s right to make an independent decision. Bottom line: Today’s potential rate hike could create a headache for Trump and the Republican Party, as it comes just ahead of a tense midterm election, with many economic warning signs flashing red.— MM Copy About the author Matty Merritt Morning Brew Become smarter in just 5 minutes Morning Brew delivers quick and insightful updates about the business world every day of the week from Wall St. to Silicon Valley. title: Canada woos investors with dozens of projects
author: Sam Klebanov
description: Prime Minister Mark Carney is pitching the world on investing C$1 trillion in Canada.
content: International Canada woos investors with dozens of projects Prime Minister Mark Carney is pitching the world on investing C$1 trillion in Canada. By Sam Klebanov September 16, 2026 • less than 3 min read TOPICS: International / International Business / Foreign Direct Investment Canada is handing the world a Cheesecake Factory-thick menu with CAD$1 trillion of investment opportunities in projects across AI, natural resources and transportation. Prime Minister Mark Carney presented it yesterday to executives managing $120 trillion in assets, who gathered in Toronto for a summit aimed at courting capital for the country amid a trade war with the US. The pitch deck Aside from touting the nation’s trade ties, educated workers, vast natural resources, and low government debt, Canada is sweetening the deal with the investment version of maple syrup: Canada is expanding a tax rule allowing write-offs of depreciating assets immediately upon investment as opposed to over the years to apply to the majority of investments—lowering the tax rate from 13% to 6.4%, which is below most developed countries. The government simplified its notoriously byzantine project approval process. What are some projects open to investment? A $10 billion AI data center and a $25 billion oil pipeline in Alberta, a synthetic graphite plant in Ontario that’ll supply battery makers, and a spaceport in Nova Scotia are among the planned ventures seeking cash. Looking ahead… officials say the deals will take 12 to 18 months to materialize. Analysts note that to improve the country’s investment attractiveness, Canada’s government has to show how the enterprises can actually deliver returns . —SK Copy About the author Sam Klebanov Morning Brew Become smarter in just 5 minutes Morning Brew delivers quick and insightful updates about the business world every day of the week from Wall St. to Silicon Valley.
